atlas.name: Atlas Finance
atlas.intro: A customer portal for an investment platform: portfolio, trades and real-time analytics on any device.
atlas.challenge: The old portal took six seconds to load, refreshed data on a timer and did not work on phones. The client team had to relaunch the product without pausing trading for a single day.
atlas.solution: We designed a new information architecture and a design system, then built the portal on Nuxt with streaming quotes over WebSocket and virtualised tables. The migration ran in stages behind feature flags, with the old and new portals live side by side.
atlas.outcome: A quarter after release the active audience grew by 140%, time to first interaction dropped from six seconds to 0.9, and support stopped receiving "frozen portfolio" tickets.

orbit.name: Orbit Market
orbit.intro: Storefront and catalogue for a marketplace with four hundred thousand products and instant search.
orbit.challenge: The catalogue on the old monolith could not survive a sale: LCP of four seconds on mobile, search answering in a second, organic traffic falling every month.
orbit.solution: We moved the storefront to Nuxt with SSR and edge caching, search migrated to Meilisearch, product cards got streaming and prioritised image loading. The backend stayed untouched — only a new API layer.
orbit.outcome: LCP on mobile is 0.7 seconds, search responds in 40 milliseconds, organic traffic grew by 62% in six months. The November sale went through without a single incident.

lumen.name: Lumen
lumen.stack: Nuxt · Nuxt UI · motion-v · Nuxt Content
lumen.intro: Landing page and documentation for a team analytics SaaS.
lumen.challenge: A complex product that had to be explained in ten seconds. The previous site converted two percent of visitors into leads and nobody knew why.
lumen.solution: We interviewed customers, rewrote the positioning and built a landing page with interactive demos and strict typography. Documentation moved to Nuxt Content in the same design language as the site.
lumen.outcome: Lead conversion rose to 9.4%, average scroll depth doubled, and the site became the main lead channel instead of cold outreach.

f1.question: How much does a website cost?
f1.answer: A landing page starts at $5,000, a corporate site at $12,000, web applications are estimated after the brief. The estimate is fixed before the start and never changes without your approval.

f2.question: How long does it take?
f2.answer: A landing page takes 4–6 weeks, a website 8–12 weeks, an application from 3 months. You will see the first working version in week two.

f3.question: What is your stack?
f3.answer: Nuxt, Vue, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS. Backend in Node.js or your stack. Everything lives in an open repository with CI and documentation.

f4.question: What about support after launch?
f4.answer: The first month after release is included. After that, a support plan with an SLA or hourly work on new tasks.

f5.question: How many revisions are included?
f5.answer: Two rounds at every stage. Usually one is enough: we agree on decisions before implementing them.
